name: Jimaku
description: Finds Japanese subtitles for anime episodes on jimaku.cc, verifies the candidate against the local file's actual timing (embedded subtitle track, or voice activity in the Japanese audio), corrects constant offsets and framerate drift, and writes the result as an external .jpn.ass / .jpn.srt sidecar. Declines rather than guessing when confidence is low. (Requires a Jimaku API key.)
overview: Japanese subtitles from Jimaku, timing-verified against your media

versions.changelog:
- Only count subtitles you picked yourself towards a series' preferred release group. A bulk run
  confirming the preference that produced it was the plugin marking its own work, and it
  compounds: whatever the first sweep landed on would bias the next episode and confirm itself
  again. Rejections still count however the file got there.
- Sweep a chosen series or season from the plugin page, rather than only whole libraries nightly.
- Show what a sweep is actually doing. The Scheduled Tasks page renders only a name and a
  percentage, so the running episode and tally now appear in the task's name there, and in full
  on the plugin page - which episode, what was attached, and why anything was declined - for a
  run started from either place. It can be stopped from there too.

- Keep a record of what was attached to each episode. The sidecar's filename is derived from the
  media file, so nothing on disk said which Jimaku upload it came from; the plugin now tracks
  every attempt, and writes the source file name into the subtitle itself.
- Treat deleting a subtitle as rejecting it. That file is no longer chosen automatically for the
  episode, and the credit it gave the series' preferred release group is taken back. Picking it
  explicitly still works.
- Remove the subtitle being replaced instead of leaving it behind under a ".1." counter, so an
  episode stops accumulating sidecars the player can choose between. Only ever a file the plugin
  recorded writing, or one carrying its own stamp.
- Add a "what's attached?" view per episode, with a button to reject the current subtitle.

- Tell the client when a subtitle is actually attached. Jellyfin's own dialog says "download
  queued" and then nothing; the plugin now sends its own message once the work is finished, and
  records the outcome in Dashboard - Activity.
- Remember which release group works for a series. Once several episodes have been served
  correctly by the same group, later episodes prefer it - but only to break a close call, never
  over a measurably better match.
- Reuse a series' Jimaku search across its episodes. Searching once per episode spent half a
  sweep's request budget re-asking a settled question.
- Cap the scheduled sweep and run it newest-first, with an option to only look at recently added
  episodes. The rate limit was always respected; a first run could still saturate it for hours.
- Pick libraries to sweep with checkboxes. The multi-select gave no visible indication of what
  was actually selected.

- Choose the timing reference by agreement between the embedded tracks, not by cue count. The
  densest track is often the group's own, carrying karaoke and signs and timed differently.
- Rank candidates on how much dialogue they actually cover, not only on how well they align.
  A subtitle that omits lines and holds them briefly no longer beats a fuller one.
- Stop demoting subtitles whose filename does not state a language; only bilingual releases
  are ranked down now.
- Identify a subtitle's language by reading it rather than by parsing its filename, so an
  untagged Japanese file is recognised and a bilingual one is caught however it is named.
- Fix the choice between the two ways of comparing timings, which preferred the one that then
  failed its own threshold and caused every candidate to be declined.
- Cache the timing reference per episode, so listing candidates and then applying one no longer
  repeats the most expensive step.
- Add Jimaku to the main menu.
